subtopics.name: Key points
points: Ecology: study of organism-environment interactions.
Biotic (living) vs abiotic (non-living) factors.
Species interactions: mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, predation, competition.
Ecosystem = biotic + abiotic; types: aquatic + terrestrial.
Structural: producers, consumers, decomposers; trophic levels.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Ecosystem = Biotic (producers + consumers + decomposers) + Abiotic (light, water, soil, gases)
Energy flow: Sun → Producer → Primary consumer → Secondary consumer → ... → Heat (unidirectional)

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: An ecosystem is a functional unit of biotic and abiotic components.
Energy flows unidirectionally through an ecosystem; nutrients cycle.
Species interact through mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, predation, and competition.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Differentiate biotic and abiotic factors.
Explain the 5 species interactions with examples.
Describe the structural aspects of a pond ecosystem.
Ecology = E-C-O (Environment + Community + Organisms).
Energy flows one way; nutrients cycle round and round.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Predation (+/-) and parasitism (+/-) both harm one partner; predation usually KILLS the prey quickly,…
Mutualism (+/+) benefits both; commensalism (+/0) benefits one, affects neither; parasitism (+/-) benefits…
Competition (-/-) harms BOTH species (interspecific); intra-specific competition is within the same species.
